([Fab Lab CITe — v1 Status & Scope](https://claude.ai/artifact/Ba79nhpu9u5uKvz8eVrrVs)) recommends
the product team **defer most of 007 for v1 and keep only the storage quota**. The team has not

**Groups B, C and D do not depend on each other.** One soft coupling, recorded rather than hidden:
the wizard (D) collects `storageQuotaMb`, whose *default of 20480* comes from B. The field already
exists and is nullable today, so D without B still works — it just offers no default.

**Until the team decides, run group A then group B.** Both are in scope under every outcome.

## Read before starting

Every item was **measured** on features 000–006, and several recurred after being written down.

1. **A rejection is a claim about a MOMENT, not about the tree.** Re-read the path and re-run the
   failing command on the current tree before rejecting. **Implementers must not `git stash`**: the
   working tree is shared with concurrent verifiers, and a stash makes it lie to every one of them.
   Use `git show HEAD:path` to compare.
2. **A module with tests and no caller is not a feature.** `lib/uploads/presign.ts` is the standing
   example on this tree — 20 passing tests, zero importers. **Every new module in this list lands in
   the same task as its first caller**, and that task greps for an importer outside its own test.
3. **A guard written against its own test's cases passes that test and fails the requirement.** Ten
   occurrences across 004–006, four of them live security defects; the newest was a `not.toContain`
   that passed because `EmptyState` carries its text in a *prop*, not in children. Put the case that
   exposes the difference **into the fixture**.
4. **A `beforeAll` throw does NOT fail a test** — it aborts the file and reports *skipped*. Any task
   touching fixtures runs the **whole** directory and reads ↓ markers as failures.
5. **A test that leaves rows behind fails somebody else's file.** `tests/content/counters.test.ts`
   reconciles the whole database — and after T007 it reconciles `storageUsedMb` too, so an upload a
   test forgets to delete is now a drift. Every fixture gets an `afterAll`.
6. **`push` rebuilds every non-production schema from the field config**, so `required: true`
   re-imposes a NOT NULL a migration dropped; a hand-written migration without its `.json` snapshot
   drifts forever. Use `./scripts/migrate-create.sh`; verify with
   `DATABASE_URI=<scratch> bash scripts/migration-drift.sh`.
7. **CI compiles WITHOUT `apps/web/payload-types.ts`.** Typecheck both ways. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`
   is on; fixture ids are `string | number` — the idiom is `as never` with the reason stated.
8. **CSS in a template literal must contain neither a backtick nor tag syntax** — symptomatic as
   esbuild's `Expected ";" but found <word>`, which reads like a TypeScript error and is not one.
   Group D writes an admin view.
9. **gitleaks flags fixture passwords on entropy.** Use the shared `fixture-password-123`.
10. **A multi-key sort MUST be an array.** The comma form is REST-only and silently sorts by nothing
    on the local API.

### What 007's own planning measured — three more, each found by review, not by a test

11. **The unspread `select` recurred one function over.** 006 learned that `buildTenantClient.find`
    does not spread its args, so a type-only `select` typechecks green and drops the bound — and
    wrote a warning comment at `find` saying so. Round 1 of this plan then passed `select` to
    `findByID`, twenty lines below the warning, where the identical trap was never closed. **A lesson
    recorded at one call site does not protect its neighbour.** T015 closes it.
12. **A framework guarantee was assumed rather than verified.** Round 1 said a custom admin view's
    404 "comes free". `AdminViewConfig` in payload 3.88 is `{ Component, exact?, meta?, path? }` —
    **no access field at all**. The view refuses itself or nothing does. Ask the installed type,
    never the plan.
13. **The host is not the tenant.** `@payloadcms/plugin-multi-tenant` sets `tenant` from a
    `defaultValue` reading **`getTenantFromCookie(req.headers)`** — the admin's tenant selector —
    and a `defaultValue` is applied during field processing, **after** `beforeOperation` has run. So
    a `beforeOperation` hook reading `args.data.tenant` on a create sees nothing. T005 measures where
    the value *does* exist, before any guard depends on it.

### Environment facts that will cost an afternoon if forgotten (T033)

- **`.next/cache/fetch-cache` can pin a host to an organization that no longer has rows.**
  `resolveTenant` caches a definite match to disk and it survives a restart. Build, then change the
  database, and every anonymous read returns zero rows — rendered as *empty states*, not errors.
  Delete `apps/web/.next/cache/fetch-cache` whenever the database changes after a build.
- **`next start` runs without the workspace `.env`.** `lib/env.ts` resolves the file relative to
  `import.meta.url`, which the bundle relocates. Export it first: `set -a; . .env; set +a`.
- **The LCP budget is CI-only** — no Chrome on `PATH`, and `payload migrate` prompts even on a fresh
  database. No task may claim to have measured it locally.

### How to verify a TEST-ONLY task

A row marked `[V]` ships **only a test**; its implementation already exists, so *"no red was
obtainable"* is not a rejection. Verify by **mutation**: break the thing the test is about, watch
that test fail with its own message, restore, watch it pass. A `[V]` test that survives every
mutation is the rejection. **Every test cites the FR it covers** — `/hef.verify` maps requirements
to tests by that token, and an uncited test leaves its FR `UNCOVERED`.
